assess.goDeeper.body.en: Explore which topology fits your organization: a sample map of each, the [org goal](term:org-goal) it serves, and its trade-offs in stable and changing markets.
assess.goDeeper.body.text: 探索哪种拓扑适合您的组织：每种拓扑的示例地图、它所服务的[组织目标](term:org-goal)，以及它在稳定和变化市场中的取舍。

assess.goal.goal.en: Given the current org design and its emerging capabilities, how well does it fit the business ambitions and organizational strategy?
assess.goal.goal.text: 考虑到当前的组织设计及其正在形成的能力，它与业务抱负和组织战略的适配程度如何？

assess.lead.en: Compare your map with the three topologies. What is this organization designed for — and does that fit your strategy?
assess.lead.text: 把您的地图与三种拓扑对照。这个组织是为什么而设计的，它与您的战略适配吗？

assess.paragraphs.0.en: Directing units decide what to build; complete teams deliver it within narrow, fixed scopes. That pattern is a [Delivery Topology](term:delivery-topology).
assess.paragraphs.0.text: Directing 单元决定要做什么；完整团队在狭窄而固定的范围内交付。这种模式就是 [Delivery Topology](term:delivery-topology)。

assess.topologies.0.fit.en: Fits stable, repeatable work. Slow to change direction.
assess.topologies.0.fit.text: 适合稳定、可重复的工作。改变方向很慢。

assess.topologies.0.summary.en: Built for utilization of specialized skills.
assess.topologies.0.summary.text: 为专业技能的利用率而建。

assess.topologies.1.fit.en: Fits known demand. Teams ship within narrowly defined areas for faster flow.
assess.topologies.1.fit.text: 适合需求已知的情况。团队在狭窄界定的领域内交付，流动更快。

assess.topologies.1.summary.en: Built for fast, predictable flow of outputs.
assess.topologies.1.summary.text: 为产出快速、可预测的流动而建。

assess.topologies.2.fit.en: Fits product R&D where user habits and market demands keep changing.
assess.topologies.2.fit.text: 适合用户习惯和市场需求不断变化的产品研发。

assess.topologies.2.summary.en: Built for innovation and adaptability, to create more value.
assess.topologies.2.summary.text: 为创新和适应性而建，以创造更多价值。

book.goDeeper.body.en: Read the method as a business novel: follow Hanna, head of HR, as she looks at her organization through the Org Topologies lens, with principles, maps and real case studies.
book.goDeeper.body.text: 把这套方法当作商业小说来读：跟随人力资源负责人 Hanna，用 Org Topologies 的视角审视她的组织，其中有原则、地图和真实案例。

book.goDeeper.kicker.text: 这本书 · 亚马逊排名第一的畅销书

design.goal.goal.en: What should this organization be optimizing for, and which strategic capabilities does it need to develop to better serve its future?
design.goal.goal.text: 这个组织应该为什么而优化，它需要发展哪些战略能力，才能更好地服务未来？

design.goalTable.rows.2.when.text: 不确定、不断变化的市场

design.goalTable.rows.3.when.en: a steady core plus a new venture
design.goalTable.rows.3.when.text: 稳定的核心加一项新业务

design.lead.en: Imagine the organization you need — without today’s limits. Choose the [org goal](term:org-goal), then sketch the target design.
design.lead.text: 设想您需要的组织，不受今天的限制。选定[组织目标](term:org-goal)，再勾画目标设计。

design.paragraphs.0.en: Don’t start from who sits where today. No topology is best; [fit for purpose](term:fit-for-purpose) is, and different parts of one company can choose different designs. In this example the goal is [adaptiveness](term:adaptiveness): everyone works as one [team of teams](term:team-of-teams) in the Driving quadrant.
design.paragraphs.0.text: 不要从今天谁坐在哪里出发。没有哪种拓扑是最好的；[适配目的](term:fit-for-purpose)才是，而且同一家公司的不同部分可以选择不同的设计。在这个例子中，目标是[适应性](term:adaptiveness)：所有人在 Driving 象限中作为一个[团队的团队](term:team-of-teams)工作。

elevate.goDeeper.body.en: Find your next small, safe step: the full [Katalog](term:katalog) by area (structure, strategy, processes), with what each kata changes.
elevate.goDeeper.body.text: 找到您的下一个小而安全的步骤：完整的 [Katalog](term:katalog)，按领域（结构、战略、流程）排列，并说明每个 Kata 改变什么。

elevate.goal.goal.en: How do we make this new org design work in practice to build the missing capabilities?
elevate.goal.goal.text: 我们如何让这个新的组织设计在实践中运转起来，以构建缺失的能力？

elevate.katas.caption.en: ONE PATH FOR THIS EXAMPLE · 4 KATAS
elevate.katas.caption.text: 本例的一条路径 · 4 个 KATA

elevate.katas.items.0.text.en: The two teams join one product group.
elevate.katas.items.0.text.text: 两个团队合并为一个产品组。

elevate.katas.items.1.text.en: One backlog for the whole product: the work mandate grows ↑
elevate.katas.items.1.text.text: 整个产品只有一个 Backlog：工作授权扩大 ↑

elevate.katas.items.2.text.en: Managers stop directing outputs; teams own the outcome.
elevate.katas.items.2.text.text: 管理者不再指挥产出；团队对成果负责。

elevate.katas.items.2.title.text: 让产品负责制围绕成果重新聚焦

elevate.katas.items.3.text.en: Everyone inspects the whole product together, every cycle.
elevate.katas.items.3.text.text: 每个周期，所有人一起检视整个产品。

elevate.lead.en: Now get the change going. [Elevating Katas](term:elevating-kata)™ are small, safe experiments that widen skills and work mandates toward the target design.
elevate.lead.text: 现在让变革起步。[Elevating Kata](term:elevating-kata)™ 是小而安全的实验，朝着目标设计拓宽技能授权和工作授权。

elevate.paragraphs.0.en: The dashed circles show the target design; the arrows show the direction of change. Run the katas, then remap and start the loop again.
elevate.paragraphs.0.text: 虚线圆圈表示目标设计；箭头表示变化的方向。运行这些 Kata，然后重新绘制地图，再开始新一轮回路。

map.goal.goal.en: Which parts of our organization contribute to creating value, and how do they interact to produce it — from idea to cash?
map.goal.goal.text: 我们组织的哪些部分在为创造价值作贡献，它们如何互动来产生价值，从想法到现金？

map.lead.en: Place every unit by its two mandates: how broad its skills are (→) and how much of the work it owns (↑).
map.lead.text: 按两项授权定位每个单元：技能有多宽（→），以及它拥有多少工作（↑）。

map.note.en: Why it matters: in a study of nearly 200 org design consultants, more than half said their clients find it hard to trace how people collaborate across units.
map.note.text: 为什么重要：在一项涉及近 200 位组织设计顾问的研究中，超过半数的人表示，客户很难理清人们如何跨单元协作。

map.paragraphs.0.en: People, teams and AI agents all go on the same map. Lines show who depends on whom. Here: a product manager and a project manager direct two complete teams of people and AI agents.
map.paragraphs.0.text: 人、团队和 AI 智能体都放在同一张地图上。连线显示谁依赖谁。这里：一位产品经理和一位项目经理指挥两个由人和 AI 智能体组成的完整团队。

map.paragraphs.1.en: This is not reproducing the org chart with titles and layers. You study the kinds of work units take on, the inputs they rely on, the outputs they produce, and how work actually flows between them.
map.paragraphs.1.text: 这不是照搬带有头衔和层级的组织架构图。您要研究的是各单元承担的工作类型、依赖的输入、产生的输出，以及工作在它们之间实际如何流动。

map.principles.0.text.en: Map where work actually happens — not how the slides say it happens.
map.principles.0.text.text: 绘制工作真正发生的地方，而不是幻灯片上说的那样。

map.principles.1.text.en: See the system as it really works today, before deciding how to improve it.
map.principles.1.text.text: 在决定如何改进之前，先看清系统今天真实的运作方式。

map.principles.2.text.en: Without curiosity, mapping quickly degenerates into justification.
map.principles.2.text.text: 没有好奇心，绘制地图很快就会沦为自我辩护。

map.pullQuote.quote.en: “Mapping does not change the organization. But without mapping, change is blind.”
map.pullQuote.quote.text: “绘制地图不会改变组织。但没有地图，变革就是盲目的。”

overview.before.en: Every organization already has a design, whether purposeful or an ad hoc accretion over the years. Org design sits between strategy and performance. **MADE** is the loop that keeps it fit, named after its four moves:
overview.before.text: 每个组织都已经有了一种设计，无论是有意为之，还是多年来临时拼凑而成。组织设计位于战略与绩效之间。**MADE** 是让它保持适配的回路，名称来自它的四个步骤：

overview.image.alt.en: Change MADE systemic: Study (Map, Assess) and Improve (Design, Elevate) around org design, between strategy and performance
overview.image.alt.text: Change MADE systemic：围绕组织设计的 Study（Map、Assess）与 Improve（Design、Elevate），位于战略与绩效之间

overview.intro.after.en: . First **study** the design you have, then **improve** toward the design you need.
overview.intro.after.text: 。先**研究**现有的设计，再**改进**到所需的设计。

overview.phases.1.steps.1.text.text: 用 [Elevating Kata](term:elevating-kata) 推动变革起步
